messages:
ria (support): FYI escalated ticket from Mira — they see timeout spikes and intermittent 403s. Console shows region label 'eu-west-1' for their app, but their auth logs show keys being validated in us-central-1. Mira pasted a sample request id: req-0a1b2c3d. Can eng take a look?

mira (customer): our app started seeing ~300-800ms p95 and occasional 403s around 2025-11-03T14:12Z. Console -> Deployment -> Region shows EU, but headers in responses say X-Serving-Region: us-central-1a. We're worried about cross-region egress costs and KMS key scope.

jordan (eng): thanks, @ria. can you drop the full raw curl and response headers from the customer? need to see x-request-id and x-routing-reason if present. also what's the model and route?

ria (support): pasted from Mira (redacted):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-App: mira-shop" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-l2.1","input":"hello"}'
```
Response headers (customer):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-Id: req-0a1b2c3d
X-Serving-Region: us-central-1a
X-Routing-Reason: fallback_capacity
X-Auth-Region: us-central-1
```
Body fine but latency higher; sometimes 403 with `X-Auth-Error: KMS_KEY_REGION_MISMATCH`.

alex (sre): :eyes: initial hypothesis: console region label is derived from control-plane placement (customer org set to eu-west) but request routing can fall back to other regions when capacity missing. fallback_capacity indicates no local pool and we routed to nearest compatible pool — looks like us-central. That explains X-Serving-Region. However the 403 + KMS error suggests their KMS keys are region-scoped and not available in us-central, so auth fails on fallback.

jordan (eng): can we reproduce with a header that forces preferred region? Try `X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1` and include `-v` to capture full trace. Also check proxy logs for that req id.

mira (customer): tried pref header, still got served from us-central. curl with `-H 'X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1'` shows X-Serving-Region unchanged.

alex (sre): reproducer steps I ran from my laptop (eu-vpn):
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
```
Response headers:
```
X-Request-Id: repro-20251103-1
X-Serving-Region: us-central-1a
X-Routing-Reason: fallback_capacity
```
Proxy log snippet (matched req):
```
2025-11-03T14:10:23Z proxy-gw-03 route-checker: route(eu-west-1) -> capacity=0 TTL=0 -> selected us-central-1a; reason=fallback_capacity; served_by=proxy-us-central-1a
```
So routing table for that model/variant is depleted in eu-west pool.

jordan (eng): OK that matches. Two action items: (1) quick mitigation: set a route pin for Mira's org to prefer dedicated eu-west pool (if available) or disable fallback to other regions for their org (requires support toggle). Ria can we do that while we investigate? (2) long-term: console UI should display actual serving region per-request (from X-Serving-Region) in the trace view. Right now console shows assigned region for the deployment only, which is misleading when fallbacks occur.

ria (support): I can toggle 'prevent-cross-region-fallback' for Mira's org temporarily. doing it now. will notify when done.

incident-bot: Auto-alert: region-fallback-anomaly detected for org mira-shop; sampled 7 fallback_capacity events in last 10m. Ticket: INC-2025-811.

mira (customer): appreciated — after the toggle we see p95 drop back to ~80ms and no 403s so far. Thanks. We'll keep monitoring.

jordan (eng): follow-ups: I will open a runtime issue to add a per-request serving-region field into our console/trace UI and add an audit view for fallback events + linked request ids. Also adding an alert rule in routing service when fallback_rate > 1% for a deployment.

alex (sre): finance note: cross-region fallback causing unexpected egress/compute costs. @billing-team please flag any invoices for mira-shop last billing cycle; label with 'suspect-cross-region-serve'.

ria (support): summarizing for ticket: cause = eu-west serving pool exhausted for rwd-l2.1 -> requests fell back to us-central -> KMS keys region-scoped caused intermittent 403; mitigation = disabled cross-region fallback for org, restored normal latency; next steps = eng to add UI visibility and routing alerts; finance to check billing. I'll attach repro logs and proxy excerpts to the ticket (INC-2025-811). :white_check_mark:
